extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies preparing NEPA documents (lead agencies), NEPA practitioners, and agency counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing Environmental Impact Statements (EISs) under NEPA, including scoping, notice content, timing, document length, incorporation by reference, public engagement, and related procedural rules. Focused on how agencies must structure EISs and related notices to satisfy CEQ regulations and statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable availability of material incorporated by reference throughout the public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials incorporated by reference must be reasonably available to the public throughout the public comment period (CEQ replaces 'inspection' with 'review' and 'within' with 'throughout').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ: ensure incorporated material, including research publications and data, is openly available and accessible while an environmental document is available for public review; availability throughout the comment period is critical to meaningful public review and comment and to section 107(c) requirements to request public comment on relevant information, studies, or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make incorporated materials available during public review even when comment not required
rubrics_metrics.description: When the regulations do not require an agency to seek public comment, material incorporated by reference must still be available while an environmental document is available for public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds 'or public review' after 'comment' to clarify availability obligation in situations where formal comment is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite publicly accessible websites as an availability mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may use publicly accessible websites as an example mechanism through which material incorporated by reference may be reasonably available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ included (and finalized) 'publicly accessible website' as an example; ensure links or web-hosting keep materials available for the full review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide digital references or hyperlinks to incorporated material
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to provide digital references, such as hyperlinks, to incorporated material or otherwise indicate how the public can access the material for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed and finalized a sentence encouraging digital references; commenters supported inclusion. Use of hyperlinks facilitates public access and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose assumptions and limitations of information relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have an obligation under §§ 1506.6 and 1502.21 for EISs to disclose any relevant assumptions or limitations of the information on which they rely, including information incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to add a distinct separate requirement specifically for incorporated reference material to disclose if cited material is outdated, disputed, or not fully proven, because existing disclosure obligations cover these concerns and a separate rule could create confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference as an efficiency tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may incorporate existing documents by reference to reduce duplicative work and ensure efficient use of agency resources, and to cut down on bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ acknowledges these benefits but did not add additional regulatory text since other regulations already emphasize efficiency (e.g., §§ 1506.2, 1506.3). Use incorporation to facilitate efficient NEPA preparation while meeting availability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presumption to incorporate State materials automatically
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no regulatory presumption that agencies can incorporate environmental studies prepared in accordance with State procedural requirements akin to NEPA; agencies may incorporate material generated by States but CEQ will not establish a presumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to create a presumption to avoid confusion; § 1501.12 allows incorporation of State-generated material and § 1506.2 promotes elimination of duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of an EIS — serve as an action‑forcing device
rubrics_metrics.description: An EIS shall 'serve as an action‑forcing device' to ensure agencies consider environmental effects of their actions in decision making (restored from 1978 regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ: this language does not require agencies to take a specific action, only that information in an EIS inform agency decisions; inclusion clarifies EISs' role in achieving NEPA's substantive policies and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: EISs are more than disclosure documents; must inform planning and decisions and involve the public
rubrics_metrics.description: An EIS must be used concurrently with other relevant information to make informed decisions and should involve the public; it is more than a mere disclosure exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added language restoring 1978 text and inserted 'involve the public' to emphasize that EISs should inform planning/decisions and facilitate public participation rather than function as a perfunctory check-the-box.

rubrics_metrics.name: EISs must state how alternatives and decisions meet NEPA and related requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs must explain how alternatives and decisions will or will not achieve the requirements of NEPA, CEQ regulations, and other environmental laws and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized changes directing lead agencies to explain in EISs the relationship between alternatives/decisions and statutory or regulatory requirements to improve transparency and decision‑usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'important' for environmental issues; reserve 'significant' for effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace occurrences of 'significant' and 'non-significant' (in some contexts) with 'important' and 'unimportant' to align usage; use 'significant' only when describing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ treats this as a clarifying, non-substantive change to improve consistency across regulations and to limit 'significant' to effect determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping should begin early and prior to issuance of the NOI where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping work should begin as soon as practicable and can and should begin prior to issuance of the Notice of Intent (NOI) to facilitate meeting statutory timeframes (e.g., two-year deadline to complete EISs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ changed 'may' to 'should' to emphasize early initiation of scoping; agencies need early scoping to gather information for meaningful public input on NOIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of scoping — solicit public input on proposed action, alternatives, and relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping is intended to receive input from the public on the proposed action and alternatives as well as other information relevant to consideration of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ moved and clarified the general purpose of scoping into § 1502.4(a) and finalized text accordingly; identify scoping topics for the NOI (see § 1502.4(e)(1)–(e)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping outreach — facilitate notification to interested or affected persons/agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must facilitate notification to persons and agencies that may be interested or affected by a proposed action as part of scoping outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ moved scoping outreach requirements into § 1502.4(b) and added an introductory sentence requiring agencies to facilitate such notification consistent with public and governmental engagement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite cooperating and participating agencies and proponents/applicants to engage
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should invite Federal, State, Tribal, and local agencies, governments, and other likely affected or interested persons (including 'any applicant') to participate as cooperating or participating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised paragraph headings and added regulatory text to make clear invitations should be extended and that invited agencies should respond in a timely manner; changed 'proponent of the action' to 'any applicant' for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify cooperating/participating agencies and information needs in the NOI
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOI must list any cooperating and participating agencies identified at the time of the NOI and must include any information those agencies require to facilitate their decisions or authorizations related to the EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added § 1502.4(e)(9) to promote early communication so lead and cooperating agencies can account for unique statutory/regulatory requirements and avoid re-issuance of a second NOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOI must request public comment on alternatives/impacts and relevant information/studies/analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with section 107(c) of NEPA, the NOI must include a request for public comment on alternatives or impacts and on relevant information, studies, or analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised paragraph (e)(7) to align with statutory language; this is part of the information to be included in NOIs to solicit meaningful public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require unique identification number for each NOI/EIS action and propagate it
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOI must include a unique identification number for tracking purposes that is carried forward in all other documents related to the action (draft and final EISs, ROD) and used in agency databases/tracking systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed and retained § 1502.4(e)(10) for better public and agency tracking of EIS progress; final rule added a clause requiring use of the ID in agency databases or tracking systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish notices of withdrawal or cancellation in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency withdraws or cancels an NOI or discontinues preparation of an EIS, it should publish a notice in the Federal Register to inform the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notices should reference the original NOI, name of the project, unique identification number, and who to contact for additional information; they need not be lengthy but should provide clear reference information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — commence EIS preparation as close as practicable and integrate NEPA early
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to commence preparation of an EIS close to the time they are developing or receive a proposal (recognizing feasibility/go-no-go stages may vary) and to integrate NEPA with planning and authorization processes early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies that feasibility analyses and 'go/no-go' stages differ across agencies; agencies have discretion to determine appropriate timing but should integrate NEPA early to improve efficiencies and outcomes (see § 1501.2(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin preparing an EIS after receiving a 'complete' application but may start earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must begin preparing an EIS after receiving a complete application, though they may elect to begin the process earlier; agencies should work together with potential applicants and other entities before receiving the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added 'complete' to paragraph (b) to clarify the baseline but retained flexibility; early coordination can improve efficiency, but CEQ declined to mandate specific completeness timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not impose uniform agency-wide deadlines for application completeness in CEQ regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ will not add specific deadlines (e.g., 30 days to determine completeness or 6 months to issue NOI) at the regulatory level because of varying agency contexts; such specifics are left to agency NEPA procedures or program regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines requests for objective measures of 'complete' at the regulation level, noting the broad applicability of CEQ regulations across diverse agencies and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS page limits set by statute — 150 pages (300 for extraordinary complexity), no exceedance mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs are subject to statutory page limits of 150 pages, or 300 pages for proposals of extraordinary complexity (excluding citations and appendices); CEQ removed any regulatory authorization to exceed these limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ removed the provision allowing a senior agency official to approve longer documents because the statute does not provide a mechanism for exceedance; agencies should adhere to statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concise EISs proportional to scope and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs should be brief, concise, and no longer than necessary; the length should be proportional to the scope and complexity of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ: page limits are maximums; agencies should not automatically use every allowable page and should avoid writing documents longer than necessary. This acknowledges some EISs may be shorter than the page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear textual edits to avoid constraining agencies' NEPA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove language that could inappropriately constrain agencies (e.g., deletes 'as interpreted in' to avoid limiting agencies whose procedures go beyond CEQ regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ removed constraining phrases so agencies can tailor their procedures to their programs and include more specific requirements and suggestions where appropriate (see § 1502.2(d) discussion).
